candidates.name: Tribological Surface Coating

candidates.failure_link: Extends spalling pre-cursor phase, shifting fault onset beyond alarm window.
candidates.cost_to_test: 5 samples, accelerated rig testing, 3 weeks duration.
candidates.standard_solution: Standard chrome alloy inner race with no additional surface treatment.
candidates.departure: Uses thin-film deposition to alter surface residual stress state.

candidates.name: Heat Treatment Optimization
candidates.mechanism: Adjust tempering cycle to increase subsurface hardness and compressive stress.
candidates.failure_link: Reduces crack initiation rate, extending spalling progression time before alarm.
candidates.cost_to_test: Two heat batches, metallographic analysis, two weeks.
candidates.standard_solution: Standard quench and temper process with fixed parameters.
candidates.departure: Modifies tempering temperature and hold time to optimize fatigue life.

candidates.name: Enhanced Cage Design
candidates.mechanism: Increase cage window area to reduce rolling element drag and heat.
candidates.failure_link: Lowers thermal load, delaying spalling onset and extending lead time.
candidates.cost_to_test: Prototype cage, thermal simulation, six weeks.
candidates.standard_solution: Standard stamped steel cage with minimal ventilation.
candidates.departure: Larger windows reduce friction, decreasing thermal spalling risk.

candidates.name: Adaptive Load Control
candidates.mechanism: Reduce fan load during low-demand periods to lower contact stress.
candidates.failure_link: Decreases spalling acceleration, extending fault development time before alarm.
candidates.cost_to_test: SCADA logic change, one-week validation in controlled conditions.
candidates.standard_solution: Fixed fan speed control independent of load demand.
candidates.departure: Dynamic load modulation based on real-time demand profile.

candidates.name: Scheduled Maintenance Protocol
candidates.mechanism: Implement condition-based maintenance based on SCADA trends.
candidates.failure_link: Detects early spalling via SCADA, extending warning time before alarm.
candidates.cost_to_test: Protocol revision, trial run, three months.
candidates.departure: Shifts from periodic to trend-driven maintenance scheduling.

candidates.failure_link: Identifies spalling pre-cursors, providing 14-day warning before alarm.

pair_against_a0plus.note: the A1 invention arm pairs against the A0+ default path for the same problem (owner R11 item 3)

a1_answer:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Deploy a gradient-boosted tree model on 1 Hz SCADA logs to detect early spalling precursors via subtle shifts in motor current variance and fan load coefficient, rather than relying on high-frequency vibration spikes. The system triggers an alert when the rolling 7-day mean of the calculated Spalling Prognostic Index (SPI) exceeds a dynamic baseline threshold, providing a 14-day warning window. This approach decouples detection from the vibration alarm, which typically trips only after significant material failure.

MECHANISM: Inner-race spalling initiates as subsurface fatigue cracking. As micro-pits grow, they cause periodic load redistribution among rolling elements, manifesting as increased current ripple and torque oscillations in the drive system. These electromechanical anomalies are captured by 1 Hz SCADA data as deviations in power consumption or motor current, appearing weeks before the structural failure generates sufficient high-frequency vibration to trigger standard sensors.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard practice uses high-frequency vibration spectral analysis (envelope detection) on 1 kHz data to confirm spalling when it is already advanced. This approach instead uses low-rate SCADA telemetry for prognostics, treating the drive's electrical behavior as a leading indicator of bearing health, thereby shifting the intervention point from reactive repair to preventive replacement.

Labeled Parameters:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Spalling Prognostic Index (SPI) = normalized deviation of 1 Hz motor current RMS from 30-day moving average (rationale: current ripple is a low-cost proxy for mechanical load fluctuations caused by spalling; calibration requires correlating SCADA current logs with post-mortem bearing inspections to define the baseline noise floor).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Alert Threshold = SPI value corresponding to 99.5th percentile of healthy-state baseline (rationale: conservative statistical boundary to limit false alarms to <2/year while capturing early spalling trends; specific value must be derived from site-specific historical SCADA data during a 6-month commissioning period).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Warning Lead Time = 14 days (User Constraint; rationale: minimum required interval for parts procurement and maintenance scheduling).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: False Alarm Rate = max 2 per year (User Constraint; rationale: balances operational disruption with predictive coverage).

INDICATOR: Spalling Prognostic Index (SPI)
THRESHOLD: 99.5th percentile of healthy baseline (ASSUMPTION)

VALIDATION PROTOCOL:
Temperature: Ambient industrial operating range (10–35 °C).
Duration: 12 months continuous monitoring.
Sample Size: n = 5 independent devices (industrial fan drives of similar class and power rating).
Data Window: 24-hour rolling window for feature extraction.
Detection Criterion: The Spalling Prognostic Index (SPI) must exceed the alert threshold for 3 consecutive days to register a valid detection.

ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Fault Prognosis via SCADA = feasible (rationale: literature demonstrates wind turbine bearing fault prognosis based solely on SCADA data, validating the use of low-rate telemetry for early fault detection in rotating machinery [doi:10.3390/s21062228]).
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Bearing Fault Prevalence = 30%-40% of total failures (rationale: highlights the critical need for early detection methods beyond standard vibration alarms [doi:10.1038/s41598-025-25083-4]).
